newsitem.title: USA: Fed watches U.S. jobless rate/inflation link-Meyer.
newsitem.headline: Fed watches U.S. jobless rate/inflation link-Meyer.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is watching the U.S. unemployment rate to see if it has dropped to a level that would be associated with inflationary pressures, Fed Governor Laurence Meyer said in a newspaper interview published on Thursday.

"The question is -- and I don't think we can run away from the question -- is the unemployment rate already so low that if it stays there inflation will rise in the future? That is the question that we have to grapple with," Meyer told Investor's Business Daily.

The U.S. unemployment rate stood at 5.1 percent in August and 5.2 percent in September. In the past, Keynesian economists have associated such low unemployment with the emergence of wage-related inflationary pressures.

"Given how low the unemployment rate is already, it is important -- imperative -- to slow growth to trend so the unemployment rate doesn't fall further," Meyer said. "But when you get to this slowdown to trend, all you do is stabilize its unemployment rate at its prevailing level."
Meyer acknowledged the Fed did not yet know the rate to which U.S. growth slowed in the third quarter.

"We do not know yet whether the third quarter was at or above trend. That's what we are tracking, to see whether the slowdown that appears to be occurring is of the nature that brings us to trend," Meyer said.

"If you had told me two years ago that the economy was going to end up with a 5.50 percent unemployment rate for a two-year period, I would have expected to see some gradual increase in inflation," Meyer added.
